teaser.en: It looks like the garden egg's wild twin, but its round yellow fruits are not eaten.

summary.en: *Mtungudza koma* is the Sodom apple, a prickly, grey-felted shrub with purple flowers and round yellow fruits. It is the wild, inedible relative of the cultivated garden egg, and its roots and leaves are used for malaria.

about.en: *Mtungudza koma* is a shrub covered in soft grey felt and armed with sharp prickles on the stems and leaves. Its flowers are purple with a yellow centre, the same shape as tomato and eggplant flowers, to which it is related. The fruits are round, about the size of a marble or larger, and turn yellow when ripe.

where.en: It grows on disturbed ground, fallow land and in bushland, often along paths and around old fields.

uses.en: The Digo of Diani boil the roots and leaves to treat malaria. The fruits are not eaten.

culture.en: The name means 'wild *tungudza*': it is seen as the inedible wild form of the cultivated garden egg.

names.en: The Digo name *mtungudza koma* is shared with Duruma and Swahili. In English it is the Sodom apple. The Mgombato dictionary records *koma* as the fruit of the doum palm, a different word, so how *koma* comes to mean 'wild' here is unclear.

mgombato: koma3 (ma) fruit of the dwarf or doum palm; koma. (See: mkoma)
sources: Pakia, M. (2005) African Traditional Plant Knowledge Today: an ethnobotanical study of the Digo at the Kenya Coast. PhD thesis, Univ. Bayreuth, Appendix III (Digo–botanical name list) & Appendix VI (name semantics). https://epub.uni-bayreuth.de/881/1/Pakia.pdf
